newsitem.title: SWEDEN: H&M says in serious talks on Finland/France.
newsitem.headline: H&M says in serious talks on Finland/France.

text.p: Swedish retailer Hennes & Mauritz(H&M) on Friday said it was in "serious discussions" over opening its first stores in Finland and France in the near future.
"We are in serious discussions," chief executive Stefan Persson told Reuters in an interview.
"Finland and France are probably new markets for Hennes & Mauritz in the foreseeable future."
He would not elaborate further on the possible timings for the new stores.
H&M currently has about 450 stores across Europe, with over 100 in Germany, its key market.
Persson said the company will have opened 55 new stores by the end of this year and planned to open another 50 in 1997 and possibly the same amount again in 1998.
He said markets with good growth potential for H&M were Germany, Austria, the Netherland, Belgium and Britain.
Persson said the company had no plans to expand beyond Europe at the moment.
"I think we have enough with our plans here in Europe," Persson said.
"Why take the risk when it is not necesssary?"
